道渴而死: Dying of thirst along the way
夸父与日逐走，入日。: Kuafu raced after the sun and reached its setting place.
饮于河、渭，河、渭不足。: He drank from the Yellow and Wei Rivers, but they were insufficient.
北饮大泽。: He went north to drink from the Great Marsh.
未至，道渴而死。: Before reaching it, he died of thirst along the way.
弃其杖，化为邓林。: His abandoned staff became Deng Forest.

本篇山列向东叙述；行文所述里数不按比例绘制。: The book describes a sequence of mountains toward the east. Distances in li are not drawn to scale.
精卫条目所属山名。: The mountain named in the account of Jingwei.
原文明确标出西北；布局只保留此相对方位。: The text explicitly specifies the northwest; the layout preserves only that relative direction.
原文记向西次序与里数；未核实前序锚点前不绘制关系线。: The text records westward progression and distances. No relation line is drawn without verifying the preceding reference point.
篇目分区，不表示单一地点。: A region representing a book, rather than a single place.
作为扶桑的相对方位参照。: A reference point for Fusang's relative direction.
章尾山的方位参照。: A directional reference for Mount Zhangwei.
赤水之北；并见西北海之外。: North of the Red River, beyond the northwestern sea.
又东三百里，曰青丘之山。: Another three hundred li east lies Mount Qingqiu.
发鸠之山，有鸟焉，其状如乌，文首、白喙、赤足，名曰精卫。: On Mount Fajiu lives a bird resembling a crow, with a patterned head, white beak and red feet. Its name is Jingwei.
海内昆仑之墟，在西北，帝之下都。: Within the seas, Kunlun lies in the northwest. It is the Celestial Ruler's lower capital.
又西三百五十里，曰玉山，是西王母所居也。: Another three hundred and fifty li west lies Mount Yu, where the Queen Mother of the West resides.
全篇依次记述东向山列。: The book describes successive eastern mountain ranges.
全篇依次记述南向山列。: The book describes successive southern mountain ranges.
全篇依次记述西向山列。: The book describes successive western mountain ranges.
全篇依次记述北向山列。: The book describes successive northern mountain ranges.
汤谷上有扶桑，十日所浴，在黑齿北。: Above Tang Valley stands Fusang, where the ten suns bathe, north of Heichi.
西北海之外，赤水之北，有章尾山。: Beyond the northwestern sea, north of the Red River, stands Mount Zhangwei.
昆仑之墟……帝之下都。九门有开明兽守之，百神之所在。: Kunlun is the Celestial Ruler's lower capital. The Kaiming beast guards its nine gates; it is a gathering place of deities.
西北海之外，赤水之北，有章尾山。有神……是烛九阴，是谓烛龙。: Beyond the northwestern sea, north of the Red River, stands Mount Zhangwei. Its deity is Zhu Jiuyin, also called Zhulong.
猿状，人面、白耳，伏行如人走。: An ape-like being with a human face and white ears; it crouches and moves as a person walks.
马状、白首，虎纹而赤尾。: Horse-like, with a white head, tiger markings and a red tail.
狐状九尾，音如婴儿。: A fox with nine tails and a cry like an infant's.
鱼身人面，声如鸳鸯。: A fish with a human face and a call like a mandarin duck's.
羊状九尾四耳，眼睛在背上。: Goat-like, with nine tails, four ears and eyes on its back.
龟状鸟首、虺尾，声如判木。: Turtle-like, with a bird's head and serpent's tail; its cry sounds like splitting wood.
雕状有角，声如婴儿。: An eagle-like creature with horns and a cry like an infant's.
状如狸而白首，音如榴榴，可以御凶。与后世天狗形象分列。: Wildcat-like, with a white head and a liuliu cry; said to ward off calamity. Kept distinct from later Tiangou traditions.
鹤状，一足，赤文青质、白喙；出现与火灾征兆相连。: A one-legged crane-like bird, blue-green with red markings and a white beak; its appearance is an omen of fire.
赤豹状，五尾一角，声如击石。: A red leopard-like creature with five tails and one horn; its cry sounds like striking stone.
状如虎而有翼，食人；与《西山经》同名异形条目分开收录。: A winged, man-eating tiger-like being. Kept separate from the differently described Qiongqi in Western Mountains.
状如牛，猬毛，音如嗥狗。: Ox-like, with hedgehog spines and a cry like a howling dog.
豚状有牙，见则年成丰盛。: A tusked, pig-like creature whose appearance foretells a plentiful harvest.
猿状白首赤足，见则有兵。: An ape-like creature with a white head and red feet; its appearance foretells war.
人面、马身，有虎纹并生鸟翼；经文另记巡行四海。: A human face, horse's body, tiger markings and bird's wings. The text also describes it patrolling the four seas.
人面虎身，九尾；经文记其司天之九部及帝之囿。: A human face and tiger's body with nine tails; it oversees heaven's nine divisions and the ruler's gardens.
羊状四角，食人。: A man-eating, goat-like creature with four horns.
蜂状而大如鸳鸯；螫中鸟兽则死。: Bee-like, as large as a mandarin duck; its sting kills birds and beasts.
鱼身有翼，苍文白首。: A winged fish with blue-green markings and a white head.
状如狸，一目三尾；其音如夺百声，可以御凶。: Wildcat-like, with one eye and three tails; its cry overpowers a hundred voices and wards off calamity.
马状白身黑尾，一角虎牙虎爪，声如鼓。: Horse-like, with a white body, black tail, one horn, tiger's teeth and claws, and a drum-like cry.
乌状、文首白喙赤足；衔木石以填东海。: Crow-like, with a patterned head, white beak and red feet; it carries wood and stones to fill the Eastern Sea.
牛状白首，一目蛇尾。: Ox-like, with a white head, one eye and a serpent's tail.
豹状长尾，人首牛耳，独目。: Leopard-like, with a long tail, human head, ox's ears and one eye.
虎首人身，衔蛇、操蛇，四蹄长肘。正文作“彊良”。: A tiger's head and human body, holding snakes in its mouth and hands, with four hooves and long elbows. The source preserves an older written form of the name Qiangliang.
赤色人面蛇身；其瞑乃晦，其视乃明。: Red, with a human face and serpent's body. Darkness falls when its eyes close; light returns when they open.
共工之臣，九首，以食于九山。: Gonggong's retainer, with nine heads that feed upon nine mountains.
九首皆人面；原文另记守昆仑九门的关系。: Nine heads, all with human faces; the text associates it with guarding Kunlun's nine gates.
状如黄囊，赤如丹火，六足四翼，浑敦无面目。: Like a yellow sack, yet red as cinnabar fire, with six feet and four wings, without a face or eyes.
鱼身而鸟翼，音如鸳鸯，见则其邑大水。: A fish with bird's wings and a mandarin duck's call; its appearance foretells flooding.
鸡状，五采有文；首、翼、背、膺、腹之文各有名义，按本篇形象收录。: Chicken-like, with five-colored markings on its head, wings, back, chest and belly, each bearing a named virtue. This entry follows the account in this book.
状如彘而人面，黄身赤尾；音如婴儿。: Pig-like, with a human face, yellow body, red tail and a cry like an infant's.
